name: Major Histocompatibility Complex Class II Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for MHC Class II Deficiency

criteria.description: Absent or markedly reduced expression of MHC class II molecules on antigen-presenting cells
Profoundly decreased CD4+ T-cell numbers in peripheral blood
History of recurrent severe bacterial, viral, and fungal infections
Identification of mutations in genes regulating MHC class II expression (e.g., CIITA, RFXANK, RFX5, RFXAP)
Variable hypogammaglobulinemia or normal immunoglobulin levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent MHC class II expression on antigen-presenting cells plus decreased CD4+ T-cell count and clinical history of recurrent infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and immunological criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent MHC class II molecule expression on antigen-presenting cells
Severe combined immunodeficiency phenotype with defective CD4 T-cell development

laboratory: Absent or severely reduced MHC class II expression on B cells, monocytes, and dendritic cells by flow cytometry
Markedly decreased CD4+ T-cell counts with normal or elevated CD8+ T-cell counts
Lymphopenia with impaired T-helper cell function
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
genetic: Mutations in CIITA, RFXANK, RFX5, or RFXAP genes affecting MHC class II transcription
other: Poor response to vaccines requiring T-helper cell function
Histopathology may show absence of MHC class II expression in lymphoid tissues

distinguishingFeatures: Absent T-cell function affecting both CD4+ and CD8+ subsets

redFlags: Early onset of severe recurrent infections
Profound CD4+ T-cell lymphopenia with absent MHC class II expression
references: Reith W, LeibundGut-Landmann S, Waldburger JM. Regulation of MHC class II gene expression by the class II transactivator. Nat Rev Immunol. 2005 Oct;5(10):793-806.
Fleisher TA. Clinical immunology and MHC class II deficiency. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2010;125(2 Suppl 2):S252-7.
